triplets.object: Eating and Appraisal Due to Emotions and Stress Questionnaire

Relations._evidence: Pearson's correlation tests revealed a negative correlation between psychological inﬂexibility and the total score on the emotional eating test (r = −0.504, p < 0.001), along with the subscales self-efﬁcacy in emotion- and stress-related eating (r = −0.303, p = 0.001), self-conﬁdence in emotion- and stress-related eating (r = −0.258, p = 0.001), and appraisal of resources and ability to cope (r = −0.647, p < 0.001).

triplets.object: Total score on the emotional eating test

Relations._evidence: When analyzing how psychological inﬂexibility is related to emotional eating and the healthy eating index, Pearson's correlation tests revealed a negative correlation between psychological inﬂexibility and the total score on the emotional eating test (r = −0.504, p < 0.001), along with the subscales self-efﬁcacy in emotion- and stress-related eating (r = −0.303, p = 0.001), self-conﬁdence in emotion- and stress-related eating (r = −0.258, p = 0.006), and appraisal of resources and ability to cope (r = −0.647, p < 0.001). However, no signiﬁcant correlations were found between psychological inﬂexibility and scores on the healthy eating index (r = −0.085, p = 0.369).
